articles.title: Vote Yes on Proposition 4: Democracy Shouldn’t Depend on Wealth
articles.author: Sharon Kyle
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. A person should not need wealthy friends to run for public office. And a voter’s influence should not depend on the size of a campaign contribution. Those principles sound basic. Yet when raising money becomes the first test of political viability, people with deep pockets gain an advantage before voters ever hear the candidates debate. Community knowledge, public service, and good ideas can take a back seat to access to donors. California’s Proposition 4, the California Fair Elections Act, offers a practical step toward changing that imbalance. On November 3, vote yes. articles.title: 100,000 California State Workers Struck Last Month
articles.author: Kari Thompson
articles.content_excerpt: State workers went on a one-day unfair labor practice strike across California on October 21, with picket lines in Sacramento, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and other cities. They’re demanding better pay, affordable health care coverage, and flexibility to work from home. This was the first strike in the history of Service Employees International Union (SEIU) Local 1000, which represents about one hundred thousand government employees, ranging from accountants to custodians to nurses at state offices, hospitals, and prisons. They have been working without a contract since July 1. Some five thousand employees were excluded from striking. Governor Gavin Newsom’s “return-to-office” mandate went into effect this past summer. articles.title: Sí, Se Puede
articles.author: Steve Appleford
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. At a vigil in downtown Los Angeles for Dolores Huerta, mourners gathered to remember the veteran labor organizer and civil rights activist with affection and awe. Behind the small crowd of dignitaries loomed a seven-story mural depicting Huerta as a young organizer, arms crossed, her face composed with quiet strength. There were tears and speeches from politicians and activists, along with repeated chants of the slogan Huerta popularized decades ago: “¡Sí, se puede!” (“Yes, we can!”). articles.title: Data Centers Shape the 2026 Midterm Elections
articles.author: Marcus Baram
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. In the final stretch of the 2026 midterm campaigns, the most potent climate issue in American politics arrived by delivery truck across the country. The average price of heating oil hit $6.23 a gallon for the week of Oct. 26, up from $3.60 a year earlier, according to the Energy Information Administration . At that price, filling a 250-gallon tank cost about $1,557 — roughly $657 more than the year before. As cold weather settled over the Northeast, Democrats turned that bill into an attack on Republican candidates. articles.title: Iran-Contra at 40
articles.author: Christian Parenti
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. On Nov. 3, 1986, almost exactly 40 years ago, a Lebanese magazine called Ash Shiraa reported that the United States, with Israel as intermediary, had clandestinely sold millions of dollars of anti-aircraft missiles to Ayatollah Khomeini’s Iran in exchange for the release of six American hostages held by Hezbollah in Lebanon. It was one of a cascade of revelations about the covert workings of the American state that came to be known as the Iran-Contra affair. Forty years on, the state too often operates along similar lines, but for a rare moment in the late 1980s, there was real accountability. articles.title: The US Electorate Is Permanently Mobilized and Unable to Move
articles.author: Corey Robin
articles.content_excerpt: Six theses on the midterm elections: Early voting tallies are through the roof . If the patterns continue, turnout is expected to match that of the midterm elections in 2018 , which saw the highest turnout rate in a midterm election since 1914. This comes in the wake of turnout for the 2020 election, which was the highest since 1900. Turnout in the 2026 midterm election is supposed to be especially high among black, Latino, and independent voters. Despite nearly a decade’s worth of record turnout, the electorate remains still roughly evenly divided, oscillating around the 50/50 mark. Even when one party manages to seize control of all the elected branches of the federal government, it doesn’t make a lasting dent in the divided nature of the electorate. articles.author: Jack Rasmus
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. The French have a saying: “Plus ca change; rien ca change”. Translated it means ‘everything changes, nothing changes’; or, depending on your French, ‘everything changes but everything remains the same’. That likely describes the current midterm 2026 US elections. Whichever party takes the House or the Senate, the policies of recent years will not change much. US foreign policy under Trump’s last two years will remain on its current disaster trajectory. And the domestic policy excesses of the past two years will remain mostly intact. articles.title: Captain Picard Was a Socialist, and So Was Patrick Stewart
articles.author: Alexander Deley
articles.content_excerpt: For those of us who grew up watching Star Trek: The Next Generation , Patrick Stewart’s death last week was an enormous loss. Stewart was an actor of extraordinary talent, commanding every scene he appeared in while bringing emotional depth to even the most imposing characters. Equally comfortable with Shakespearean tragedy, science fiction, and comedy, Stewart could do it all. There was also something about his premature baldness that aged him — adding to his already impressive natural gravitas — but also gave him an ageless quality over the decades. Whether he was performing Shakespeare onstage or appearing in sci-fi shlock like the naked-space-vampire thriller Lifeforce (1985), he always fully embodied the characters that he played.
